query: Who was Nephi?

documents.text: And now there were some among the people, who said that Nephi was a prophet.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 9:40** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records five men verifying Nephi’s prophecy by finding Chief Judge Seezoram dead. Seantum is confronted, found with blood, confesses, and Nephi and the five are freed. Some believe Nephi is a prophet; others call him a god.

documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 1:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. Unbelievers set a day to kill believers unless Samuel’s sign occurs; Nephi prays and the Lord promises the sign and Christ’s birth. Night has no darkness and a new star appears. Many repent and are baptized; debate over the law of Moses ends. Later years are mostly peaceful but Gadianton robbers grow through Nephite dissenters and Zoramite influence among Lamanite youth.

Nephi, keeper of the records, does not return to Zarahemla and cannot be found. In the thirteenth year wars intensify with numerous Gadianton robbers; converted Lamanites unite with Nephites, are numbered as Nephites, and fight for safety and worship. Fighting continues through years 14–15 with shifting advantages and increasing afflictions.

documents.text: And thus ended the eleventh year of the judges, the Lamanites having been driven out of the land, and the people of Ammonihah were destroyed; yea, every living soul of the Ammonihahites was destroyed, and also their great city, which they said God could not destroy, because of its greatness.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 16:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Lamanite armies destroying Ammonihah, taking captives, and Zoram with sons Lehi and Aha seeking Alma’s guidance. Alma prophesies the Lamanite route; the Nephite army meets them east of Sidon near Manti, rescues all captives, and drives the Lamanites away. Ammonihah becomes the Desolation of Nehors. After years of peace, Alma, Amulek, and others preach repentance, condemn sins, and teach Christ’s coming, death, resurrection, and appearance after resurrection.

documents.text: But as to the people that were in the land of Ammonihah, they yet remained a hard-hearted and a stiffnecked people; and they repented not of their sins, ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil; for they were of the profession of Nehor, and did not believe in the repentance of their sins.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 15:15** from the **Book of Mormon**. Alma establishes a church in Sidom and ordains priests and teachers as many are baptized. Ammonihah remains unrepentant. Amulek loses wealth and family support; Alma and Amulek return to Zarahemla.

documents.text: And now it came to pass, before the Nephites could raise a sufficient army to drive them out of the land, they had destroyed the people who were in the city of Ammonihah, and also some around the borders of Noah, and taken others captive into the wilderness.

documents.text: And it came to pass after they had thus suffered for many days, (and it was on the twelfth day, in the tenth month, in the tenth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi) that the chief judge over the land of Ammonihah and many of their teachers and their lawyers went in unto the prison where Alma and Amulek were bound with cords.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 14:23** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 29 verses and records many in Ammonihah believing Alma and Amulek, while others bind them and accuse them before the chief judge. Zeezrom confesses guilt and is cast out. Believers, their wives and children, and scriptures are burned, and Alma and Amulek are imprisoned, beaten, mocked, and deprived. On the twelfth day Alma prays; they break their cords, an earthquake destroys the prison and kills their persecutors, and they escape as the people flee.

documents.text: Behold, I said that the city of Ammonihah had been rebuilt. I say unto you, yea, that it was in part rebuilt; and because the Lamanites had destroyed it once because of the iniquity of the people, they supposed that it would again become an easy prey for them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 49:3** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records Lamanite armies approaching rebuilt Ammonihah and being thwarted by Moroni’s fortifications. The Lamanites retreat to attack the city of Noah, where Lehi commands and defenses include banks, ditches, and guarded entrances. Lamanite assaults fail; chief captains are slain and over a thousand die, while no Nephites are killed and about fifty are wounded. Amalickiah reacts with anger and oaths, while Nephites give thanks; the year ends with peace and church prosperity under Helaman, Shiblon, Corianton, and Ammon.

documents.text: And it came to pass that Alma and Amulek, Amulek having forsaken all his gold, and silver, and his precious things, which were in the land of Ammonihah, for the word of God, he being rejected by those who were once his friends and also by his father and his kindred;

documents.text: And now behold, I have somewhat to say concerning the people of Ammon, who, in the beginning, were Lamanites; but by Ammon and his brethren, or rather by the power and word of God, they had been converted unto the Lord; and they had been brought down into the land of Zarahemla, and had ever since been protected by the Nephites.

It notes Nephite dissensions that allow Lamanites to take western cities. It recounts the people of Ammon’s oath against bloodshed, Helaman preventing them from breaking it, and 2,000 of their sons covenanting to fight under Helaman, who marches to the southwest borders.

documents.text: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Genesis 50:3** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Joseph mourning Jacob, having Israel embalmed, and receiving Pharaoh’s permission to bury him in Canaan at Machpelah; a large Egyptian company accompanies the funeral and mourns at Atad. Joseph’s brothers fear revenge and seek forgiveness; Joseph reassures and provides for them. The chapter notes Joseph’s 110-year life, descendants through Ephraim and Manasseh, his prophecy of Israel’s return, his oath about his bones, and his death and embalming in Egypt.

This chapter contains 36 verses and records Ammon visiting Lamoni’s queen, declaring Lamoni is not dead, and Lamoni rising the next day. Lamoni testifies he has seen the Redeemer; the king, queen, Ammon, and servants fall prostrate by the Spirit. Abish gathers the people; a man trying to kill Ammon falls dead. Abish raises the queen and king, who teach the crowd. Many believe, are baptized, and a church is established among the Lamanites.

documents.text: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 20:26** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Mary Magdalene finding the stone removed and reporting to Peter and the other disciple, who inspect the empty tomb and linen cloths. Mary sees two angels and then Jesus, who tells her to report to the disciples. Jesus appears to the disciples, shows his wounds, commissions them, gives the Holy Ghost, and speaks of remitting or retaining sins. Thomas doubts, then sees Jesus and confesses him. The chapter states the purpose of the written signs.

documents.text: Command therefore that the sepulchre be made sure until the third day, lest his disciples come by night, and steal him away, and say unto the people, He is risen from the dead: so the last error shall be worse than the first.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 27:64** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 66 verses and records the chief priests and elders delivering Jesus to Pilate; Judas returning thirty pieces of silver, hanging himself, and the purchase of the potter’s field. Pilate offers Barabbas, washes his hands, and hands Jesus over for scourging and crucifixion. Soldiers mock Jesus; Simon of Cyrene carries the cross; Jesus is crucified at Golgotha with two thieves amid darkness and temple signs. Joseph of Arimathea buries Jesus, and the tomb is sealed and guarded.

documents.text: And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Corinthians 15:4** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 58 verses and records Paul’s summary of the gospel: Christ dies, is buried, rises, and appears to Cephas, the Twelve, many brethren, James, the apostles, and Paul. It argues that denying resurrection makes faith and preaching vain, then outlines resurrection order and Christ’s reign until death is destroyed. It mentions baptism for the dead, warns against corrupting associations, explains resurrection bodies, and commands steadfast labor.

documents.text: And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 9:9** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records Saul obtaining letters to arrest disciples in Damascus, encountering a heavenly light and Jesus, becoming blind, and being healed and baptized through Ananias. Saul preaches in Damascus, escapes a plot, and is accepted in Jerusalem through Barnabas before being sent to Tarsus. It also covers church growth, Peter healing Aeneas in Lydda, raising Tabitha in Joppa, and staying with Simon the tanner.

documents.text: Then Jesus six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was which had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.

It covers Jesus’ entry into Jerusalem with palm branches, Greeks seeking him, and teachings on his coming death, serving him, and being the light. A heavenly voice speaks; Jesus explains judgment and belief, notes unbelief fulfilling Isaiah, and affirms speaking the Father’s commandment.

documents.text: And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceeding sorry.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 17:23** from the **New Testament**. Jesus commands silence until after his resurrection and explains Elias as John the Baptist. He heals a boy possessed by a devil, teaches faith, prayer, and fasting, foretells his betrayal, death, and resurrection in Galilee, and provides tribute money in Capernaum via a coin found in a fish.

documents.text: To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days, and speaking of the things pertaining to the kingdom of God:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 1:3** from the **New Testament**. Peter addresses about 120 disciples about Judas’ death and the “field of blood,” cites Psalms, and Matthias is chosen by lot to replace Judas.

documents.text: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 12:40** from the **New Testament**. Jesus heals many and commands silence, with an Isaiah citation. He casts out a demon from a blind, mute man, answers Beelzebub accusations, warns about blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, teaches about words and fruit, refuses a sign except Jonah, describes returning unclean spirits, and identifies doers of God’s will as family.

documents.text: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 18:33** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records Jesus’ parables of the persistent widow and the unjust judge, and the Pharisee and the publican praying in the temple. Jesus predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection, then heals a blind beggar near Jericho.

documents.text: Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

Jesus appears to two disciples on the road to Emmaus, explains scriptures, is recognized in breaking bread, and vanishes. He appears to the gathered disciples, shows his hands and feet, eats food, commissions preaching repentance and remission of sins, promises power from on high, and ascends near Bethany.

documents.text: After two days was the feast of the passover, and of unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 14:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 72 verses and records priests and scribes plotting to kill Jesus, a woman anointing him in Bethany, and Judas arranging betrayal. Jesus directs Passover preparations, predicts a betrayer, and institutes bread and cup at the meal. He foretells disciples’ scattering and Peter’s denial, prays in Gethsemane, and is arrested. Jesus is tried before the high priest and council, condemned, mocked, and beaten. Peter denies Jesus three times before the cock crows twice and weeps.

documents.text: And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.

documents.text: For he taught his disciples, and said unto them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill him; and after that he is killed, he shall rise the third day.

He casts out a dumb and deaf spirit, teaches prayer and fasting, and instructs on humility, receiving children, not forbidding others, rewards, avoiding offenses, warnings of hell, and salt and peace.

documents.text: Him God raised up the third day, and shewed him openly;

He preaches Jesus’ ministry, death, resurrection, and commanded witness. The Holy Ghost falls on Gentile hearers; Peter orders their baptism.

query: Who was the first prophet of the Restoration?

documents.text: And again, in connection with this quotation I will give you a quotation from one of the prophets, who had his eye fixed on the restoration of the priesthood, the glories to be revealed in the last days, and in an especial manner this most glorious of all subjects belonging to the everlasting gospel, namely, the baptism for the dead; for Malachi says, last chapter, verses 5th and 6th: Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 128:17** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records instructions on baptism for the dead and the required record-keeping: ward recorders and a general church recorder document ordinances with dates, names, and witnesses. It links earthly records with heavenly records and cites Revelation 20, Matthew 16, 1 Corinthians 15, and Malachi 4. It references angelic restorations (Moroni, Michael, Peter, James, John) and urges preparing a temple book of the dead’s records.

documents.text: And also with Elias, to whom I have committed the keys of bringing to pass the restoration of all things spoken by the mouth of all the holy prophets since the world began, concerning the last days;
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 27:6** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus teaching to give alms, pray, and fast in secret rather than for public display, including the Lord’s Prayer and commands to forgive others. It contrasts earthly and heavenly treasures, discusses the single eye and serving God rather than mammon, and instructs not to be anxious about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 6:6** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus teaching to give alms, pray, and fast in secret rather than for public display, including the Lord’s Prayer and commands to forgive others. It contrasts earthly and heavenly treasures, discusses the single eye and serving God rather than mammon, and instructs not to be anxious about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: But behold, I say unto you that ye must pray always, and not faint; that ye must not perform any thing unto the Lord save in the first place ye shall pray unto the Father in the name of Christ, that he will consecrate thy performance unto thee, that thy performance may be for the welfare of thy soul.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 32:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 9 verses and records Nephi teaching what to do after entering “the way”: receive the Holy Ghost, which enables speaking with the tongue of angels and brings the words of Christ. He commands readers to feast on Christ’s words, ask and knock for understanding, and states this is the doctrine of Christ until Christ manifests in the flesh. Nephi urges prayer always, warning against the evil spirit, and instructs praying to the Father in Christ’s name to consecrate actions.

documents.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father who is in secret; and thy Father, who seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 13:6** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus’ instructions on giving alms, praying, and fasting in secret rather than for public praise. It gives a model prayer and commands forgiveness of others. It warns against storing earthly treasures, serving God and Mammon, and having an evil eye. Jesus charges the twelve to minister and teaches not to worry about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: And said unto Jeremiah the prophet, Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee, and pray for us unto the LORD thy God, even for all this remnant; (for we are left but a few of many, as thine eyes do behold us:)
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 42:2** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Judah’s remnant, led by Johanan, asking Jeremiah to pray for guidance and pledging obedience. After ten days Jeremiah delivers the LORD’s word: remain in the land and God will build and plant them, show mercy, and protect them from the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, sword, famine, and pestilence will overtake them; they are warned not to go and are accused of dissembling.

documents.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 6:13** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus teaching to give alms, pray, and fast in secret rather than for public display, including the Lord’s Prayer and commands to forgive others. It contrasts earthly and heavenly treasures, discusses the single eye and serving God rather than mammon, and instructs not to be anxious about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen, for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 13:7** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Jesus’ instructions on giving alms, praying, and fasting in secret rather than for public praise. It gives a model prayer and commands forgiveness of others. It warns against storing earthly treasures, serving God and Mammon, and having an evil eye. Jesus charges the twelve to minister and teaches not to worry about food, drink, or clothing, but to seek God’s kingdom first.

documents.text: If, when evil cometh upon us, as the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we stand before this house, and in thy presence, (for thy name is in this house,) and cry unto thee in our affliction, then thou wilt hear and help.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Chronicles 20:9** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 37 verses and records Moab, Ammon, and Mount Seir invading Judah, with their host at En-gedi. Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast, prays in the temple, and Jahaziel prophesies Judah need not fight. Judah marches from Tekoa with singers; the enemy armies destroy each other. Judah gathers spoil three days, blesses God in the valley of Berachah, and returns to Jerusalem. Jehoshaphat’s reign is summarized; he allies with Ahaziah to build Tarshish ships at Ezion-geber, and the ships are broken after Eliezer’s prophecy.

documents.text: I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Timothy 2:8** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 15 verses and covers exhortations to offer prayers, intercessions, and thanksgiving for all people, including rulers, so believers may live quietly and godly. It states God desires all to be saved, affirms one God and one mediator, Christ Jesus, who gives himself as a ransom, and notes Paul’s commission to teach Gentiles. It instructs men to pray without anger and women to dress modestly, learn quietly, not teach or exercise authority over men, referencing Adam and Eve, and mentions salvation in childbearing with continuing faith, charity, holiness, and sobriety.

documents.text: O Lord God Almighty, hear us in these our petitions, and answer us from heaven, thy holy habitation, where thou sittest enthroned, with glory, honor, power, majesty, might, dominion, truth, justice, judgment, mercy, and an infinity of fulness, from everlasting to everlasting.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 109:77** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 80 verses and records a dedicatory prayer for the Kirtland temple. It thanks God for commanding the house and asks Him to accept, sanctify, and keep His presence there, excluding unclean things. It petitions for repentance, spiritual gifts, angelic protection, and power for missionaries, with outcomes for receptive or rejecting cities. It requests deliverance for Missouri exiles, mercy on nations and rulers, gathering of Israel, remembrance of Joseph Smith and church leaders, and final salvation and resurrection.

documents.text: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 21:36** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 38 verses and records Jesus observing the widow’s two mites and comparing her gift to the rich. He foretells the temple’s destruction and gives signs of coming deception, wars, disasters, and persecution. He predicts Jerusalem surrounded, desolated, and its people slain or captive. He describes cosmic signs and the Son of man’s coming, gives the fig tree parable, and commands watchfulness and prayer while teaching in the temple and lodging on the Mount of Olives.

documents.text: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ephesians 6:18** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 24 verses and covers instructions for children to obey parents and for fathers to nurture without provoking; servants to obey masters sincerely and masters to forbear threatening. It urges believers to be strong, put on the whole armor of God against spiritual powers, and pray continually. Paul requests prayer for bold gospel speech as an imprisoned ambassador, sends Tychicus with news, and closes with peace and grace.

documents.text: Yet if they bethink themselves in the land whither they are carried captive, and turn and pray unto thee in the land of their captivity, saying, We have sinned, we have done amiss, and have dealt wickedly;
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Chronicles 6:37** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 42 verses and records Solomon blessing Israel at the temple dedication, recounting God’s choice of Jerusalem and promise to David, and placing the ark in the house. Solomon prays with hands spread, asking God to hear prayers toward the temple, forgive sins, judge oaths, restore after defeat, send rain, relieve famine and plague, hear foreigners, grant victory, and show mercy in captivity. He closes with petitions for priests and the anointed.

documents.text: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.
documents.context: The following passage is from **James 5:15** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records warnings to rich oppressors about coming judgment, hoarded wealth, and withheld wages. It commands believers to be patient for the Lord’s coming, avoid grumbling, and follow examples of prophets and Job. It forbids swearing oaths, instructs prayer in affliction and praise in joy, and directs elders to pray and anoint the sick. It includes confession, effective prayer, Elijah’s prayers about rain, and restoring erring sinners.

documents.text: O God, the Eternal Father, we ask thee in the name of thy Son, Jesus Christ, to bless and sanctify this bread to the souls of all those who partake of it; that they may eat in remembrance of the body of thy Son, and witness unto thee, O God, the Eternal Father, that they are willing to take upon them the name of thy Son, and always remember him, and keep his commandments which he hath given them, that they may always have his Spirit to be with them. Amen.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moroni 4:3** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 3 verses and records the manner elders and priests administer the sacrament bread to the church according to Christ’s commandments, kneeling with the congregation and praying to the Father in Christ’s name to bless and sanctify the bread, for participants to remember Christ’s body, take upon them his name, always remember him, keep his commandments, and have his Spirit with them.

query: What does scripture say about repentance?

documents.text: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 11:18** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records Peter defending his visit with uncircumcised Gentiles by recounting the Joppa vision, the Spirit’s command, Cornelius’s message from an angel, and the Holy Ghost falling on Gentiles; Jerusalem believers accept Gentile repentance. It covers scattered disciples preaching in Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, Barnabas and Saul teaching a year, disciples first called Christians, Agabus predicting famine, and Antioch sending relief to Judea.

documents.text: And wo unto him to whom he shall say this, for it shall be unto him that will do iniquity, and he cannot be saved; therefore, for this cause, that men might be saved, hath repentance been declared.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 12:22** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records Mormon’s reflections on human unsteadiness: people prosper, forget God, and require chastening by afflictions, death, famine, and pestilence. It states God’s power to command earth, mountains, waters, and the length of day, and to curse hidden treasures and individuals for iniquity. It declares repentance as the means of salvation and contrasts final outcomes of everlasting life versus damnation.

documents.text: And now, my brethren, I would that, after ye have received so many witnesses, seeing that the holy scriptures testify of these things, ye come forth and bring fruit unto repentance.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 34:30** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Amulek teaching the Zoramites about Christ’s coming and the need for an infinite, eternal atonement that fulfills the law of Moses. He explains mercy and justice, urges faith unto repentance, continual prayer in all places, and charity to the needy. He warns against procrastinating repentance, describes the state after death, and exhorts humility, taking Christ’s name, resisting the devil, patience in afflictions, and hope of rest.

documents.text: Now I say unto you that ye must repent, and be born again; for the Spirit saith if ye are not born again ye cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven; therefore come and be baptized unto repentance, that ye may be washed from your sins, that ye may have faith on the Lamb of God, who taketh away the sins of the world, who is mighty to save and to cleanse from all unrighteousness.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 7:14** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records Alma speaking at Gideon after leaving the judgment-seat, expressing hope the people are faithful, and urging repentance and preparation for the Son of God. He prophesies Christ’s birth to Mary at Jerusalem and describes his suffering, death, and taking sins and infirmities. Alma commands being born again, baptism, covenant keeping, humility, patience, prayer, gratitude, and having faith, hope, and charity, then pronounces blessings and peace.

documents.text: And he heard a voice from heaven, saying: Enoch, my son, prophesy unto this people, and say unto them—Repent, for thus saith the Lord: I am angry with this people, and my fierce anger is kindled against them; for their hearts have waxed hard, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes cannot see afar off;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moses 6:27** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 68 verses and records Adam calling his sons to repent; Seth’s birth and worship; a book of remembrance and priesthood; genealogies from Adam to Enoch; increasing wickedness, wars, and secret works; Enoch’s prophetic call, visions, and preaching in the land of Cainan; and God’s instructions to Adam on repentance, baptism in Jesus Christ’s name, the Holy Ghost, and Adam’s baptism and spiritual rebirth.

documents.text: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mark 1:15** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 45 verses and records John the Baptist preaching repentance and baptizing in the Jordan, foretelling one greater. Jesus is baptized, the Spirit descends, and a heavenly voice speaks; Jesus is tempted in the wilderness. After John’s imprisonment Jesus preaches in Galilee, calls Simon, Andrew, James, and John, teaches in Capernaum, casts out an unclean spirit, heals Simon’s mother-in-law and many others, prays alone, preaches through Galilee, and cleanses a leper.

documents.text: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 19:4** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Paul’s ministry in Ephesus, where about twelve disciples baptized into John’s baptism are baptized in Jesus’ name and receive the Holy Ghost by laying on of hands. Paul teaches in the synagogue, then daily in Tyrannus’s school for two years; miracles occur and the sons of Sceva fail at exorcism. Converts confess and burn magic books. Demetrius incites a riot over Diana shrines; Gaius and Aristarchus are seized, and the townclerk dismisses the assembly.

documents.text: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judæa, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 26:20** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records Paul’s defense before King Agrippa, with Festus and Bernice present. Paul recounts his Pharisaic life, persecution of believers, and his Damascus road encounter with Jesus, receiving a commission to witness to Jews and Gentiles. He states he preaches repentance and fulfillment of Moses and the prophets, including Christ’s suffering and resurrection. Festus challenges him; Agrippa responds. They conclude Paul is not guilty but is bound by his appeal to Caesar.

documents.text: And the Father said: Repent ye, repent ye, and be baptized in the name of my Beloved Son.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 31:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Nephi’s plain statement of the doctrine of Christ. He references the Lamb of God’s baptism, the descent of the Holy Ghost, and the strait and narrow path. He commands repentance, baptism in Christ’s name, receiving the Holy Ghost and baptism of fire, and warns against later denial. He teaches pressing forward, feasting on Christ’s words, and enduring to the end to gain eternal life.

documents.text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 15:7** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 32 verses and records Jesus teaching parables after Pharisees and scribes complain that he receives sinners. It includes the lost sheep sought by its owner, the lost coin found by a woman, and the prodigal son who wastes his inheritance, returns, and is received by his father. The elder son objects, and the father explains rejoicing over the restored son.

documents.text: And behold, ye do know of yourselves, for ye have witnessed it, that as many of them as are brought to the knowledge of the truth, and to know of the wicked and abominable traditions of their fathers, and are led to believe the holy scriptures, yea, the prophecies of the holy prophets, which are written, which leadeth them to faith on the Lord, and unto repentance, which faith and repentance bringeth a change of heart unto them—
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 15:7** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records Samuel warning the Nephites to repent or face desolation, mourning, and destruction despite signs and wonders. He contrasts them with many Lamanites who keep the law of Moses, seek to convert others, believe scripture, repent, and bury weapons. He states the Lord prolongs and will later restore the Lamanites though they are scattered, but will utterly destroy unrepentant Nephites.

documents.text: For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Corinthians 7:10** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 16 verses and records Paul urging believers to cleanse themselves and pursue holiness, defending his conduct toward the Corinthians. He describes troubles in Macedonia and comfort received through Titus’s arrival and report of their desire, mourning, and zeal. Paul explains his earlier letter caused temporary sorrow leading to repentance, contrasts godly and worldly sorrow, notes their renewed obedience, and expresses joy, comfort, and confidence in them.

documents.text: Yea, and it bringeth to pass the condition of repentance, that whosoever repenteth the same is not hewn down and cast into the fire; but whosoever repenteth not is hewn down and cast into the fire; and there cometh upon them again a spiritual death, yea, a second death, for they are cut off again as to things pertaining to righteousness.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 14:18** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite prophesying signs of the Son of God’s birth in five years, including a night without darkness and a new star, and calling the people to repent. He also prophesies signs of Christ’s death: three days of darkness, thunderings, earthquakes, broken rocks, tempests, desolated cities, and opened graves with saints appearing. He teaches resurrection, repentance versus condemnation, and human agency to choose good or evil.

documents.text: Yea, open your mouths and they shall be filled, saying: Repent, repent, and prepare ye the way of the Lord, and make his paths straight; for the kingdom of heaven is at hand;
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 33:10** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 18 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to Ezra and Northrop to preach the gospel at the “eleventh hour,” labor in a corrupted vineyard, and help gather the elect. It commands them to declare repentance, baptism by water, and the baptism of fire and the Holy Ghost, emphasizing faith in Christ. It references church establishment, articles and covenants, confirmation by laying on of hands, and use of the Book of Mormon and scriptures. It urges prayerful readiness for Christ’s coming.

documents.text: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 17:30** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records Paul and Silas preaching in Thessalonica, some believing, and opposition leading to Jason being accused and released on security. Paul and Silas go to Berea, where many examine Scripture and believe, but Thessalonian Jews stir trouble. Paul is sent to Athens, disputes in synagogue and marketplace, and speaks at the Areopagus about the Creator, repentance, and resurrection; some mock, others believe, including Dionysius and Damaris.

documents.text: Behold, my son, this thing ought not to be; for repentance is unto them that are under condemnation and under the curse of a broken law.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moroni 8:24** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records an epistle from Mormon to Moroni addressing disputes about baptizing little children. Mormon reports seeking the Lord and teaches that little children are alive in Christ, not accountable for sin, and need no repentance or baptism. He defines baptism as for accountable sinners unto remission of sins and warns against perverting this doctrine. He also mentions conflict with the Lamanites and Nephite pride, spiritual decline, and impending destruction.

documents.text: And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Matthew 3:2** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records John the Baptist preaching repentance in the wilderness of Judea, baptizing in the Jordan as people confess sins, and warning Pharisees and Sadducees to produce worthy fruit. John describes one coming after him who baptizes with the Holy Ghost and fire and brings judgment. Jesus comes from Galilee, is baptized by John, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a heavenly voice identifies Jesus as God’s beloved Son.

documents.text: And him that repenteth not of his sins, and confesseth them not, ye shall bring before the church, and do with him as the scripture saith unto you, either by commandment or by revelation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 64:12** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to church elders to overcome the world, repent, and forgive all men, with directions for church discipline of the unrepentant. It names Joseph Smith and affirms keys with conditions of obedience, addresses sins of Ezra Booth, Isaac Morley, and Edward Partridge, and gives instructions about farms, business, and moving to Zion. It teaches sacrifice and tithing, warns of burning upon the wicked, outlines stewardship and judging in Zion, and foretells Zion’s flourishing and gathering.

documents.text: But if ye will repent and return unto the Lord your God I will turn away mine anger, saith the Lord; yea, thus saith the Lord, blessed are they who will repent and turn unto me, but wo unto him that repenteth not.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Helaman 13:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 39 verses and records Samuel the Lamanite preaching repentance at Zarahemla from the city wall after being cast out. He prophesies destruction within 400 years unless the Nephites repent and have faith in Jesus Christ. He warns Zarahemla, Gideon, and surrounding cities, foretells curses on the land and “slippery” hidden treasures, condemns persecuting prophets and trusting flattering teachers, and declares probation ending through procrastination.

documents.text: And of tenets thou shalt not talk, but thou shalt declare repentance and faith on the Savior, and remission of sins by baptism, and by fire, yea, even the Holy Ghost.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 19:31** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Jesus Christ declaring His authority as Alpha and Omega, the final judgment, and the need for repentance to avoid suffering. It defines “eternal/endless punishment” as God’s punishment and recounts Christ’s suffering in Gethsemane. It commands repentance, confession, prayer, meekness, and preaching repentance and baptism. It forbids coveting and seeking life, directs supporting Book of Mormon printing, paying printer debts, imparting property, and preaching widely.

query: What is the role of the Holy Ghost?

documents.text: And the Holy Ghost beareth record of the Father and me; and the Father giveth the Holy Ghost unto the children of men, because of me.
documents.context: The following passage is from **3 Nephi 28:11** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records Jesus asking the Nephite disciples what they desire after his departure. Nine request to end their ministry and come to him at age seventy-two; three desire to remain and bring souls to Christ and are promised they will not taste death. They are transfigured, forbidden to reveal what they see, and continue ministering, baptizing, and giving the Holy Ghost. They escape prisons, pits, furnaces, and beasts unharmed; Mormon notes their future ministry among Gentiles, Jews, and Israel and explains their bodily change until judgment.

documents.text: And again, it is given by the Holy Ghost to some to know the diversities of operations, whether they be of God, that the manifestations of the Spirit may be given to every man to profit withal.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 46:16** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records instructions for church meetings to be conducted by the Holy Spirit, commanding members not to exclude people from public, sacrament, or confirmation meetings, with restrictions on partaking after trespass until reconciliation. It warns against deception and commands prayer and thanksgiving. It lists spiritual gifts (testimony of Christ, belief, administration, operations, wisdom, knowledge, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning, tongues, interpretation) and assigns leaders to discern gifts.

documents.text: To some it is given by the Holy Ghost to know that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and that he was crucified for the sins of the world.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 46:13** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records instructions for church meetings to be conducted by the Holy Spirit, commanding members not to exclude people from public, sacrament, or confirmation meetings, with restrictions on partaking after trespass until reconciliation. It warns against deception and commands prayer and thanksgiving. It lists spiritual gifts (testimony of Christ, belief, administration, operations, wisdom, knowledge, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning, tongues, interpretation) and assigns leaders to discern gifts.

documents.text: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 14:26** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Jesus consoling his disciples, promising to prepare a place in the Father’s house and to return. He answers Thomas about the way to the Father, teaches Philip about seeing the Father through him, and promises believers will do works and have prayers answered in his name. He commands keeping his commandments, promises the Comforter/Holy Ghost, gives peace, foretells his departure, and mentions the prince of this world.

documents.text: The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's; the Son also; but the Holy Ghost has not a body of flesh and bones, but is a personage of Spirit. Were it not so, the Holy Ghost could not dwell in us.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 130:22** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records teachings about seeing the Savior as a man, continued sociality after this life, and a personal appearing of the Father and Son. It addresses differing reckoning of time by planets, angels ministering only to their own earth, and God’s residence as a Urim and Thummim; the sanctified earth and individual white stones function similarly. It includes prophecy of bloodshed beginning in South Carolina, a statement about Joseph Smith possibly seeing the Son of Man, principles of intelligence gained in mortality, blessings tied to obedience to law, and the embodied nature of the Father and Son versus the Holy Ghost.

documents.text: The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth; and thy dominion shall be an everlasting dominion, and without compulsory means it shall flow unto thee forever and ever.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 121:46** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 46 verses and records a plea to God regarding persecutions, followed by comfort that adversity is temporary and endurance brings exaltation. It pronounces woes and judgments on those who falsely accuse, oppress, and murder the Saints, including loss of priesthood rights. It promises revealed knowledge in the dispensation of the fulness of times and teaches that priesthood power operates only through righteousness, persuasion, meekness, charity, and without compulsion.

documents.text: For the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Luke 12:12** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 59 verses and records Jesus warning disciples against Pharisaic hypocrisy, urging fear of God, confession of him, and reliance on the Holy Ghost in trials. He refuses to arbitrate an inheritance dispute, warns against covetousness, and gives the parable of the rich fool. He teaches not to worry, to seek God’s kingdom, give alms, and be watchful like servants. He speaks of accountability, coming division, discerning the times, and reconciling with an adversary before judgment.

documents.text: And it shall come to pass, that if you shall ask the Father in my name, in faith believing, you shall receive the Holy Ghost, which giveth utterance, that you may stand as a witness of the things of which you shall both hear and see, and also that you may declare repentance unto this generation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 14:8** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 11 verses and records the Lord declaring a great work coming forth and urging heed to His word. It calls willing laborers to harvest and promises salvation for enduring and keeping commandments. It commands seeking to establish Zion, asking in faith, and receiving the Holy Ghost to witness and declare repentance. Jesus Christ identifies Himself and states He will bring the fulness of the gospel from the Gentiles to Israel, calling David to assist.

documents.text: And again, to some it is given by the Holy Ghost to know the differences of administration, as it will be pleasing unto the same Lord, according as the Lord will, suiting his mercies according to the conditions of the children of men.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 46:15** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records instructions for church meetings to be conducted by the Holy Spirit, commanding members not to exclude people from public, sacrament, or confirmation meetings, with restrictions on partaking after trespass until reconciliation. Hyrum is told not to preach until called, to study and obtain the word, keep peace, and be patient while translation proceeds. It affirms revelation and Jesus Christ’s identity and promises to believers power to become sons of God.

query: What is the covenant of baptism?

documents.text: Yea, I say unto you come and fear not, and lay aside every sin, which easily doth beset you, which doth bind you down to destruction, yea, come and go forth, and show unto your God that ye are willing to repent of your sins and enter into a covenant with him to keep his commandments, and witness it unto him this day by going into the waters of baptism.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Alma 7:15** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records Alma speaking at Gideon after leaving the judgment-seat, expressing hope the people are faithful, and urging repentance and preparation for the Son of God. He prophesies Christ’s birth to Mary at Jerusalem and describes his suffering, death, and taking sins and infirmities. Alma commands being born again, baptism, covenant keeping, humility, patience, prayer, gratitude, and having faith, hope, and charity, then pronounces blessings and peace.

documents.text: And when he had said these words, the Spirit of the Lord was upon him, and he said: Helam, I baptize thee, having authority from the Almighty God, as a testimony that ye have entered into a covenant to serve him until you are dead as to the mortal body; and may the Spirit of the Lord be poured out upon you; and may he grant unto you eternal life, through the redemption of Christ, whom he has prepared from the foundation of the world.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 18:13** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Alma teaching Abinadi’s words privately, including Christ, resurrection, and redemption. Believers gather at the waters of Mormon, covenant to bear burdens, mourn, comfort, and serve God, and Alma baptizes about 204, beginning the church of God. Alma ordains priests and commands repentance, faith, unity, Sabbath observance, weekly worship, self-supporting priests, and giving to the needy. King Noah discovers them, sends an army, and Alma leads about 450 people into the wilderness.

documents.text: And ye will also know that ye are a remnant of the seed of Jacob; therefore ye are numbered among the people of the first covenant; and if it so be that ye believe in Christ, and are baptized, first with water, then with fire and with the Holy Ghost, following the example of our Savior, according to that which he hath commanded us, it shall be well with you in the day of judgment. Amen.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mormon 7:10** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 10 verses and records Mormon addressing the spared remnant of the house of Israel. He states they are Israel and must repent to be saved, lay down weapons, and stop shedding blood unless God commands. He urges belief in Jesus Christ’s death and resurrection, teaching resurrection and judgment. He commands repentance and baptism, referencing additional records, and identifies them as Jacob’s remnant of the first covenant.

documents.text: Now I say unto you, if this be the desire of your hearts, what have you against being baptized in the name of the Lord, as a witness before him that ye have entered into a covenant with him, that ye will serve him and keep his commandments, that he may pour out his Spirit more abundantly upon you?

It states the oath and covenant of the priesthood, warns the church to repent and remember the Book of Mormon, and commands preaching, baptism, and avoiding boasting of signs. It gives missionary instructions, judgments on rejecting cities, consecration guidance, and assignments to Newel K. Whitney.

documents.text: And now, because of the covenant which ye have made ye shall be called the children of Christ, his sons, and his daughters; for behold, this day he hath spiritually begotten you; for ye say that your hearts are changed through faith on his name; therefore, ye are born of him and have become his sons and his daughters.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 5:7** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 15 verses and records King Benjamin asking his people if they believe his words; they affirm faith, report a change of heart through the Spirit, and agree to covenant to obey God. Benjamin declares the covenant acceptable, calls them children of Christ, and commands them to take upon them Christ’s name and retain it without transgression. He contrasts right- and left-hand outcomes and urges steadfast good works.

documents.text: Herein is glory and honor, and immortality and eternal life—The ordinance of baptism by water, to be immersed therein in order to answer to the likeness of the dead, that one principle might accord with the other; to be immersed in the water and come forth out of the water is in the likeness of the resurrection of the dead in coming forth out of their graves; hence, this ordinance was instituted to form a relationship with the ordinance of baptism for the dead, being in likeness of the dead.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 128:12** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records instructions on baptism for the dead and the required record-keeping: ward recorders and a general church recorder document ordinances with dates, names, and witnesses. It links earthly records with heavenly records and cites Revelation 20, Matthew 16, 1 Corinthians 15, and Malachi 4. It references angelic restorations (Moroni, Michael, Peter, James, John) and urges preparing a temple book of the dead’s records.

documents.text: And again, by way of commandment to the church concerning the manner of baptism—All those who humble themselves before God, and desire to be baptized, and come forth with broken hearts and contrite spirits, and witness before the church that they have truly repented of all their sins, and are willing to take upon them the name of Jesus Christ, having a determination to serve him to the end, and truly manifest by their works that they have received of the Spirit of Christ unto the remission of their sins, shall be received by baptism into his church.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 20:37** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. It covers basic doctrines of creation, fall, atonement, repentance, baptism, and endurance. It gives requirements and wording for baptism and the sacrament prayers, outlines duties and authority of elders, priests, teachers, and deacons, sets conference and ordination procedures, and provides rules for membership records, discipline, children’s blessings, and letters of standing.

documents.text: This is my covenant, which ye shall keep, between me and you and thy seed after thee; Every man child among you shall be circumcised.

Abram is renamed Abraham, and Sarai is renamed Sarah. Circumcision is instituted as the covenant sign for all males. God promises Sarah bears Isaac and blesses Ishmael with twelve princes. Abraham circumcises himself, Ishmael, and his household.

documents.text: I might have rendered a plainer translation to this, but it is sufficiently plain to suit my purpose as it stands. It is sufficient to know, in this case, that the earth will be smitten with a curse unless there is a welding link of some kind or other between the fathers and the children, upon some subject or other—and behold what is that subject? It is the baptism for the dead. For we without them cannot be made perfect; neither can they without us be made perfect. Neither can they nor we be made perfect without those who have died in the gospel also; for it is necessary in the ushering in of the dispensation of the fulness of times, which dispensation is now beginning to usher in, that a whole and complete and perfect union, and welding together of dispensations, and keys, and powers, and glories should take place, and be revealed from the days of Adam even to the present time. And not only this, but those things which never have been revealed from the foundation of the world, but have been kept hid from the wise and prudent, shall be revealed unto babes and sucklings in this, the dispensation of the fulness of times.

It commands parents in Zion to teach faith, repentance, prayer, Sabbath keeping, and baptize children at age eight; rebukes idleness and greed; directs Oliver Cowdery to deliver these sayings.

documents.text: The person who is called of God and has authority from Jesus Christ to baptize, shall go down into the water with the person who has presented himself or herself for baptism, and shall say, calling him or her by name: Having been commissioned of Jesus Christ, I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Moses warns against idolatry and self-assured disobedience, listing curses, land devastation, exile, and nations’ questions; revealed law is to be obeyed.

Enoch sees Satan’s power, God and Enoch weeping, the Flood with Noah, the Son of Man’s crucifixion and resurrection, last-days tribulations, the New Jerusalem, and a millennial rest.

documents.text: And he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved, and he that believeth not, and is not baptized, shall be damned.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 112:29** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to Thomas B. Marsh, acknowledging his prayers, correcting him, forgiving his sins, and commanding him to preach to Gentiles and Jews and remain in Zion. It warns of coming wrath, commands worldwide preaching, baptism, and faithfulness, and affirms priesthood keys in the dispensation of fulness of times.

query: What does scripture say about obedience?

documents.text: Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Colossians 3:22** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records exhortations to seek things above with Christ, put to death sinful practices, and put off anger, malice, and lying while putting on the new person. It lists virtues such as mercy, kindness, humility, patience, forgiveness, love, peace, thankfulness, and worshipful teaching. It gives household commands for wives, husbands, children, fathers, and servants, urging wholehearted service to the Lord and impartial judgment for wrongdoing.

documents.text: Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ;
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ephesians 6:5** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 24 verses and covers instructions for children to obey parents and for fathers to nurture without provoking; servants to obey masters sincerely and masters to forbear threatening. It urges believers to be strong, put on the whole armor of God against spiritual powers, and pray continually. Paul requests prayer for bold gospel speech as an imprisoned ambassador, sends Tychicus with news, and closes with peace and grace.

documents.text: And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that the LORD hath said will we do, and be obedient.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Exodus 24:7** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 18 verses and records Moses being called up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders to worship, while Moses alone approaches the LORD. Moses reports the LORD’s words, writes them, builds an altar and twelve pillars, and sacrifices offerings. Blood is sprinkled on the altar and people as covenant confirmation. The leaders see God and eat. Moses ascends Sinai with Joshua to receive stone tablets; Aaron and Hur oversee the people. A cloud and glory cover the mountain; Moses remains forty days and nights.

documents.text: If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Isaiah 1:19** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Isaiah’s vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. It indicts Israel’s rebellion, moral corruption, and desolation, and rejects hypocritical sacrifices and assemblies. It commands repentance, justice for the oppressed, and care for the fatherless and widow. It contrasts promised cleansing and restoration of Zion with judgment on rebels and idolaters.

documents.text: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Samuel 15:22** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Samuel commanding Saul to destroy Amalek completely. Saul musters Israel at Telaim, warns the Kenites to depart, defeats Amalek from Havilah to Shur, but spares King Agag and the best livestock. God tells Samuel he rejects Saul for disobedience. Samuel confronts Saul at Gilgal, declares obedience above sacrifice, and announces the kingdom is torn from Saul. Samuel executes Agag, returns to Ramah, and no longer visits Saul.

documents.text: For your obedience is come abroad unto all men. I am glad therefore on your behalf: but yet I would have you wise unto that which is good, and simple concerning evil.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Romans 16:19** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 27 verses and records Paul commending Phebe of the church at Cenchrea and instructing the Romans to receive and assist her. He sends greetings to many believers and households in Rome, including Priscilla and Aquila and their house church, and relays greetings from his companions. He commands mutual greeting, warns against divisive deceivers, promises God will bruise Satan, and closes with a doxology about the revealed gospel.

documents.text: Whether it be good, or whether it be evil, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee; that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 42:6** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Judah’s remnant, led by Johanan, asking Jeremiah to pray for guidance and pledging obedience. After ten days Jeremiah delivers the LORD’s word: remain in the land and God will build and plant them, show mercy, and protect them from the king of Babylon. If they go to Egypt, sword, famine, and pestilence will overtake them; they are warned not to go and are accused of dissembling.

documents.text: Which I commanded your fathers in the day that I brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, from the iron furnace, saying, Obey my voice, and do them, according to all which I command you: so shall ye be my people, and I will be your God:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 11:4** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records the LORD commanding Jeremiah to proclaim the covenant to Judah and Jerusalem, warning of a curse for disobedience. It reports Judah and Israel breaking the covenant through idolatry, including altars to Baal, and announces unavoidable calamity and rejected prayers. Jeremiah learns of a plot against him. The LORD pronounces judgment on the men of Anathoth who seek Jeremiah’s life.

documents.text: Behold, the Lord requireth the heart and a willing mind; and the willing and obedient shall eat the good of the land of Zion in these last days.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 64:34** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records the Lord’s counsel to church elders to overcome the world, repent, and forgive all men, with directions for church discipline of the unrepentant. It names Joseph Smith and affirms keys with conditions of obedience, addresses sins of Ezra Booth, Isaac Morley, and Edward Partridge, and gives instructions about farms, business, and moving to Zion. It teaches sacrifice and tithing, warns of burning upon the wicked, outlines stewardship and judging in Zion, and foretells Zion’s flourishing and gathering.

documents.text: And the people said unto Joshua, The LORD our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Joshua 24:24** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 33 verses and records Joshua gathering Israel at Shechem, recounting God’s acts from Terah and Abraham through the exodus, wilderness, and conquest. Joshua commands the people to fear and serve the LORD, put away foreign gods, and choose whom to serve. Israel pledges obedience; Joshua makes a covenant, writes it, and sets a stone witness. It records Joshua’s death and burial, Israel’s continued service, Joseph’s bones buried at Shechem, and Eleazar’s death.

documents.text: Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Acts 5:29** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 42 verses and records Ananias and Sapphira selling land, withholding part of the price, being confronted by Peter for lying, and dying, causing fear in the church. It covers apostles doing signs and healings in Jerusalem, including Peter’s shadow. The Sadducees imprison the apostles; an angel frees them to teach in the temple. They appear before the council; Peter testifies of Jesus. Gamaliel advises restraint; the apostles are beaten, warned, and continue preaching daily.

documents.text: As the nations which the LORD destroyeth before your face, so shall ye perish; because ye would not be obedient unto the voice of the LORD your God.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 8:20** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Moses exhorting Israel to keep God’s commandments to live and possess the land. It recalls the forty years in the wilderness, including testing, chastening, manna, preserved clothing and feet, and water from rock amid serpents and drought. It describes the promised land’s resources and commands blessing God after eating. It warns against forgetting God, crediting wealth to oneself, idolatry, and disobedience, with perishing like displaced nations.

documents.text: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and ye shall be my people: and walk ye in all the ways that I have commanded you, that it may be well unto you.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 7:23** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 34 verses and records the LORD’s message to Jeremiah to preach at the temple gate in Jerusalem, calling Judah to amend conduct, execute justice, and stop oppression, bloodshed, theft, adultery, false oaths, and idolatry. query: What do scriptures say about prophets being rejected?

documents.text: And it came to pass that the prophets were rejected by the people, and they fled unto Com for protection, for the people sought to destroy them.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ether 11:2** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 23 verses and records prophets warning King Com’s people to repent; the people reject them and seek to kill them, so they flee to Com. It recounts reigns and conflicts under Shiblom, Seth, Ahah, Ethem, Moron, and Coriantor, including wars, famine, pestilence, and executions of prophets. Secret combinations fuel rebellions, overthrows, and long captivities. Prophets also foretell utter destruction and another people possessing the land. Coriantor begets Ether.

documents.text: For behold, the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep. For behold, ye have closed your eyes, and ye have rejected the prophets; and your rulers, and the seers hath he covered because of your iniquity.
documents.context: The following passage is from **2 Nephi 27:5** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records prophecies about Gentiles and Jews in the last days, divine judgments, and nations fighting Zion. It describes the coming forth of a sealed book, its delivery to an unlearned man, and the role of three and other witnesses. It notes the learned refuse to read a sealed book, and the Lord commands the sealed portion kept. It covers a “marvelous work,” exposure of secret works, and future restoration where the deaf and blind receive understanding and Jacob’s children sanctify God.

documents.text: For behold, the Spirit of the Lord ceaseth soon to strive with them; for behold, they have rejected the prophets, and Jeremiah have they cast into prison. And they have sought to take away the life of my father, insomuch that they have driven him out of the land.
documents.context: The following passage is from **1 Nephi 7:14** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records the Lord commanding Nephi and his brothers to return to Jerusalem to bring Ishmael’s family so the sons can marry. Ishmael’s household joins them, but Laman, Lemuel, and some of Ishmael’s children rebel and want to return. Nephi warns of Jerusalem’s destruction; his brothers bind him, but he prays and is freed. Ishmael’s family pleads; the rebels repent, are forgiven, pray, and all return to Lehi’s tent, offering sacrifices.

documents.text: Wherefore, he shall bring forth his words unto them, which words shall judge them at the last day, for they shall be given them for the purpose of convincing them of the true Messiah, who was rejected by them; and unto the convincing of them that they need not look forward any more for a Messiah to come, for there should not any come, save it should be a false Messiah which should deceive the people; for there is save one Messiah spoken of by the prophets, and that Messiah is he who should be rejected of the Jews.

He states the Messiah comes 600 years after Lehi leaves Jerusalem and is Jesus Christ. Nephi teaches salvation through Christ, preservation of the record, grace, and keeping Moses’s law until fulfilled.

documents.text: For behold, they have rejected the words of the prophets. Wherefore, if my father should dwell in the land after he hath been commanded to flee out of the land, behold, he would also perish. Wherefore, it must needs be that he flee out of the land.

Laman and Lemuel beat Nephi and Sam; an angel commands them to return and promises deliverance.

documents.text: And as for those who are at Jerusalem, saith the prophet, they shall be scourged by all people, because they crucify the God of Israel, and turn their hearts aside, rejecting signs and wonders, and the power and glory of the God of Israel.

query: How is the gathering of Israel described across scripture?

documents.text: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Micah 2:12** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records a woe against those who plan evil, covet fields, seize houses, and oppress families. The LORD announces judgment, lamentation over lost land, and exclusion from allotment in the congregation. The people reject prophecy and commit violence, dispossessing women and children. A command to depart is given. False prophets are noted. The LORD promises to assemble Jacob’s remnant, lead them out, and go before them with their king.

documents.text: We believe in the literal gathering of Israel and in the restoration of the Ten Tribes; that Zion (the New Jerusalem) will be built upon the American continent; that Christ will reign personally upon the earth; and, that the earth will be renewed and receive its paradisiacal glory.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Articles of Faith 1:10** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records thirteen Articles of Faith: belief in the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; accountability for personal sin; salvation through Christ’s Atonement by gospel obedience; faith, repentance, baptism, and laying on of hands; divine calling and authority; church offices; spiritual gifts; scripture (Bible and Book of Mormon); continuing revelation; gathering of Israel, Zion, and Christ’s reign; religious freedom; civic obedience; and moral virtues and doing good.

documents.text: Hear the word of the LORD, O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Israel will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Jeremiah 31:10** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records the LORD’s promise to be God to Israel, gather the remnant from exile, restore Ephraim and Judah, and bring rejoicing in Zion. It mentions Rachel weeping in Ramah, calls Israel to return with waymarks, and declares individual responsibility for sin. It announces a new covenant with Israel and Judah, with the law written in hearts and sins forgiven. It also foretells Jerusalem rebuilt with defined boundaries and made holy.

documents.text: And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Isaiah 27:12** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records the LORD punishing Leviathan, a song of a protected vineyard, and Israel/Jacob taking root and bearing fruit. It contrasts measured discipline with devastation of a fortified city, calls for purging iniquity by removing idolatrous altars and images, and foretells Israel gathered from the river to Egypt, with exiles from Assyria and Egypt returning to worship in Jerusalem.

documents.text: Thus saith the Lord GOD; When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Ezekiel 28:25** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 26 verses and records prophecies against the prince and king of Tyre for pride, wealth, and claiming divinity, foretelling invasion by foreigners, death, and a lament describing former splendor in Eden and expulsion for iniquity and violent trade. It also prophesies judgment on Zidon by pestilence and sword, and promises Israel’s gathering, secure dwelling in Jacob’s land, and safety from surrounding enemies.

Zion laments being forgotten, but the Lord remembers and restores her children through Gentile help, and contends against oppressors.

documents.text: And after the house of Israel should be scattered they should be gathered together again; or, in fine, after the Gentiles had received the fulness of the Gospel, the natural branches of the olive tree, or the remnants of the house of Israel, should be grafted in, or come to the knowledge of the true Messiah, their Lord and their Redeemer.

The LORD promises gathering from nations, one king “David,” cleansing from idols, obedience to statutes, an everlasting covenant of peace, and a permanent sanctuary among them.

documents.text: And again, how oft would I have gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, yea, O ye people of the house of Israel, who have fallen; yea, O ye people of the house of Israel, ye that dwell at Jerusalem, as ye that have fallen; yea, how oft would I have gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens, and ye would not.

query: How do scriptures describe the resurrection of the dead?

documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 15:20** from the **Book of Mormon**. He defines Christ’s “seed” as prophets and believers who heed their words. He quotes Isaiah on publishing peace and salvation. He teaches resurrection, a first resurrection for prophets, the obedient, the ignorant, and little children, and excludes willful rebels. He foresees salvation proclaimed to all nations and Zion/Jerusalem restored.

documents.text: And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:

This chapter contains 58 verses and records Paul’s summary of the gospel: Christ dies, is buried, rises, and appears to Cephas, the Twelve, many brethren, James, the apostles, and Paul. It argues that denying resurrection makes faith and preaching vain, then outlines resurrection order and Christ’s reign until death is destroyed. It mentions baptism for the dead, warns against corrupting associations, explains resurrection bodies, and commands steadfast labor.

documents.text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
