It addresses brotherly love, urging increase, quiet living, personal work, and honest conduct before outsiders. It explains hope for those who have died: the Lord’s coming, the dead in Christ rising first, and the living caught up to meet him, for mutual comfort.

It outlines end-time judgments, angels and trumpets, the Millennium, Michael’s battle, and rules for the School of the Prophets, including salutations and washing of feet.

Spirits return to God; the righteous enter paradise and rest, and the wicked enter darkness and misery. Alma distinguishes spirit states from bodily resurrection, describes restoration of body and soul, and judgment according to works.

documents.text: By these things we know that there is a God in heaven, who is infinite and eternal, from everlasting to everlasting the same unchangeable God, the framer of heaven and earth, and all things which are in them;
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 20:17** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 84 verses and records the organization of the Church of Christ (6 April 1830), naming Joseph Smith and Oliver Cowdery as first and second elders, and recounting angelic ministry and translation of the Book of Mormon. It covers basic doctrines of creation, fall, atonement, repentance, baptism, and endurance. It gives requirements and wording for baptism and the sacrament prayers, outlines duties and authority of elders, priests, teachers, and deacons, sets conference and ordination procedures, and provides rules for membership records, discipline, children’s blessings, and letters of standing.

documents.text: Wherefore, he is possessor of all things; for all things are subject unto him, both in heaven and on the earth, the life and the light, the Spirit and the power, sent forth by the will of the Father through Jesus Christ, his Son.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 50:27** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 46 verses and records the Lord warning elders about false spirits, hypocrisy, and deception in the church. It instructs that preaching and receiving must be by the Spirit of truth, and that what does not edify is not of God. It teaches testing spirit manifestations by prayer in Jesus’s name and acting without railing. It promises increasing light, purification, and authority, calls Wakefield, Pratt, and Corrill to strengthen churches, corrects Partridge, and exhorts watchfulness.

documents.text: He comprehendeth all things, and all things are before him, and all things are round about him; and he is above all things, and in all things, and is through all things, and is round about all things; and all things are by him, and of him, even God, forever and ever.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 88:41** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 141 verses and records the Lord’s instructions to assembled elders about the Holy Spirit of promise, the light of Christ, resurrection, and laws governing celestial, terrestrial, and telestial kingdoms. It describes earth’s sanctification and cosmic order, gives a parable of laborers, and commands prayer, sanctification, study, and organizing a school and house of God. It outlines end-time judgments, angels and trumpets, the Millennium, Michael’s battle, and rules for the School of the Prophets, including salutations and washing of feet.

documents.text: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth,
documents.context: The following passage is from **Exodus 34:6** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records the LORD instructing Moses to hew new stone tablets and meet Him on Sinai, where the LORD proclaims His name and renews covenant terms. Commands include rejecting covenants and intermarriage with Canaanites, destroying idols, keeping feasts, redeeming firstborn, Sabbath rest, and bringing firstfruits. Moses fasts forty days, receives the commandments, and returns with a shining face, using a veil before Israel.

documents.text: But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Psalms 86:15** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records David’s prayer for God to hear, preserve, and show mercy to a poor and needy servant who trusts in him. It affirms God’s goodness, forgiveness, and uniqueness above other gods, and anticipates all nations worshiping him. The psalm asks for instruction to walk in God’s truth, offers praise, mentions deliverance from death, and seeks help against proud and violent enemies, requesting a confirming sign.

documents.text: And whatsoever they shall speak when moved upon by the Holy Ghost shall be scripture, shall be the will of the Lord, shall be the mind of the Lord, shall be the word of the Lord, shall be the voice of the Lord, and the power of God unto salvation.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 68:4** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records a commission to Orson Hyde and other elders to preach worldwide, speak by the Holy Ghost, baptize, recognize signs, and seal converts. It outlines calling and rights of bishops, including descendants of Aaron, and trial procedures before the First Presidency. It commands parents in Zion to teach faith, repentance, prayer, Sabbath keeping, and baptize children at age eight; rebukes idleness and greed; directs Oliver Cowdery to deliver these sayings.

documents.text: He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 32:4** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 52 verses and records the Song of Moses: a summons to heaven and earth, recounting the LORD’s care for Israel, Israel’s corruption and idolatry, and announced judgments by famine, sword, and scattering. It affirms the LORD’s vengeance and mercy, calls Israel to teach and obey the law, and commands Moses to ascend Mount Nebo in Abarim to view Canaan and die for the Meribah-Kadesh trespass.

documents.text: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **John 4:24** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 54 verses and records Jesus leaving Judea for Galilee through Samaria, speaking with a Samaritan woman at Jacob’s well in Sychar about living water, worship, and his identity as the Christ. The woman testifies, and many Samaritans believe; Jesus stays two days. In Galilee he returns to Cana and heals a nobleman’s son in Capernaum by word.

documents.text: For I know that God is not a partial God, neither a changeable being; but he is unchangeable from all eternity to all eternity.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Moroni 8:18** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records an epistle from Mormon to Moroni addressing disputes about baptizing little children. Mormon reports seeking the Lord and teaches that little children are alive in Christ, not accountable for sin, and need no repentance or baptism. He defines baptism as for accountable sinners unto remission of sins and warns against perverting this doctrine. He also mentions conflict with the Lamanites and Nephite pride, spiritual decline, and impending destruction.

documents.text: Believe in God; believe that he is, and that he created all things, both in heaven and in earth; believe that he has all wisdom, and all power, both in heaven and in earth; believe that man doth not comprehend all the things which the Lord can comprehend.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 4:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records King Benjamin’s people falling down, pleading for mercy through Christ’s atoning blood, and receiving joy and remission of sins. Benjamin commands belief in God, repentance, humility, prayer, and steadfast faith. He instructs them to live peaceably, teach children, and succor the poor by sharing substance, feeding, clothing, and visiting the sick, in wisdom and order, returning borrowed goods, watching thoughts, words, and deeds, and keeping commandments to avoid perishing.

documents.text: For the LORD your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 10:17** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 22 verses and records Moses hewing new stone tablets, making a wooden ark, and receiving again the ten commandments. It notes Israel’s journeys, Aaron’s death at Mosera, and Eleazar succeeding him. The LORD separates Levi to carry the ark and minister without land inheritance. Moses recounts forty days on the mount, then commands Israel to fear, love, serve, obey, and love the stranger.

documents.text: The LORD is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Psalms 145:17** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records David’s continual praise of the LORD as king, urging daily blessing of his name and declaring his unsearchable greatness. It recounts God’s mighty acts, goodness, righteousness, mercy, and compassion. It covers proclamation of God’s everlasting kingdom, his help for the fallen, provision of food, and satisfaction of living creatures. It states God hears those who call in truth, saves those who fear him, preserves those who love him, and destroys the wicked.

documents.text: And they are one God, yea, the very Eternal Father of heaven and of earth.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 15:4** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Abinadi teaching that God comes among men as Father and Son, suffers, is crucified, and overcomes death to intercede and redeem. He defines Christ’s “seed” as prophets and believers who heed their words. He quotes Isaiah on publishing peace and salvation. He teaches resurrection, a first resurrection for prophets, the obedient, the ignorant, and little children, and excludes willful rebels. He foresees salvation proclaimed to all nations and Zion/Jerusalem restored.

documents.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD:
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 6:4** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Moses commanding Israel to keep God’s statutes in the promised land, affirming the LORD as one and commanding love for Him with all heart, soul, and might. It instructs teaching these words to children and displaying them on hand, forehead, doorposts, and gates. It warns against forgetting God after prosperity, following other gods, and tempting Him at Massah, and directs explaining the exodus and commandments to future children.

documents.text: Having ascended into heaven, having the bowels of mercy; being filled with compassion towards the children of men; standing betwixt them and justice; having broken the bands of death, taken upon himself their iniquity and their transgressions, having redeemed them, and satisfied the demands of justice.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Mosiah 15:9** from the **Book of Mormon**. This chapter contains 31 verses and records Abinadi teaching that God comes among men as Father and Son, suffers, is crucified, and overcomes death to intercede and redeem. He defines Christ’s “seed” as prophets and believers who heed their words. He quotes Isaiah on publishing peace and salvation. He teaches resurrection, a first resurrection for prophets, the obedient, the ignorant, and little children, and excludes willful rebels. He foresees salvation proclaimed to all nations and Zion/Jerusalem restored.

documents.text: Which Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are one God, infinite and eternal, without end. Amen.

documents.text: We believe in God, the Eternal Father, and in His Son, Jesus Christ, and in the Holy Ghost.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Articles of Faith 1:1** from the **Pearl of Great Price**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records thirteen Articles of Faith: belief in the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; accountability for personal sin; salvation through Christ’s Atonement by gospel obedience; faith, repentance, baptism, and laying on of hands; divine calling and authority; church offices; spiritual gifts; scripture (Bible and Book of Mormon); continuing revelation; gathering of Israel, Zion, and Christ’s reign; religious freedom; civic obedience; and moral virtues and doing good.

documents.text: For God doth not walk in crooked paths, neither doth he turn to the right hand nor to the left, neither doth he vary from that which he hath said, therefore his paths are straight, and his course is one eternal round.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 3:2** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records the Lord’s declaration that God’s purposes cannot be frustrated and that human transgression causes loss of privileges. Joseph is reproved for fearing man, transgressing commandments, and delivering sacred translation materials to a wicked man. He is commanded to repent to remain called and retain his gift. The section states the work will continue and explains the plates are preserved to bring knowledge of the Savior to various peoples, especially the Lamanites.

documents.text: Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the LORD he is God; there is none else beside him.
documents.context: The following passage is from **Deuteronomy 4:35** from the **Old Testament**. This chapter contains 49 verses and records Moses exhorting Israel to obey statutes without adding or diminishing, recalling Baal-peor and Horeb where the Ten Commandments are given. He warns against idolatry and worship of heavenly bodies, foretells exile for corruption, and promises mercy if they seek and obey God. Moses appoints three cities of refuge east of Jordan: Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan, and notes the law’s setting near Beth-peor.

documents.text: And gave unto them commandments that they should love and serve him, the only living and true God, and that he should be the only being whom they should worship.
documents.context: The following passage is from **D&C 20:19** from the **Doctrine and Covenants**.
